disclaimer: This report lists observations about a codebase. Not an assessment of compliance with any regulation. Risk classification under the EU AI Act is a legal determination made by the operator, not a tool output. Every rule in this report is UNMEASURED: no precision figure exists for it yet. Absence of a finding is not evidence of safety.

findings.title: Emotion or biometric inference on persons

recommendation.summary: Remove the inference or restrict it to a documented, lawful use with a legal basis and an Annex III review; emotion recognition at work or in education and biometric categorisation of protected characteristics are listed practices under Art. 5.
alternatives: remove the inference or restrict it to a medical or safety use with a documented legal basis
replace emotion inference with explicit, user-stated preferences
an Annex III conformity review before deployment
aisafe: nothing here applies; the control is removing or scoping the inference

known_failure_modes: text-only sentiment analysis is not counted: the EU definition of emotion recognition rests on biometric data
a library imported for a demo counts as use; DetectFaces without Emotions does not
whether the inference happens in a workplace or an education setting is read from the lint rule's words (employee, student), not from the deployment
findings.notes: emotion or affect inference signal (affect:hume). Whether this practice falls under Art. 5, Art. 50 or Annex III of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 is a legal determination made by the operator, not a tool output. The finding reports what the code and the prompts say.

recommendation.summary: Delete any instruction to claim humanity and state the AI nature at first interaction and whenever asked; AIDisclosureGuard flags a response that claims to be human and can append the disclosure on the output stage.
alternatives: delete the instruction and state the AI nature at first interaction
a UI banner at session start plus a disclosure on every channel the bot speaks through

package.leaves_open: AIDisclosureGuard flags a response that claims to be human and can append the disclosure text on the output stage; a prompt that instructs the model to claim humanity is deleted by hand, and disclosure shown by the UI is outside the guard.

known_failure_modes: a named persona (Ava) is not concealment; the regex needs a human claim or a concealment verb
a disclosure delivered by the UI rather than the code is reported as absent
the no-disclosure sub-finding is unit-level and LOW: it says no disclosure symbol was found, not that none is shown
